content.text: An example from an application proposing to collect clinical and MRI data from human subjects.
content.label: content

content.text: If any of the proposed research in the application involves the generation of scientific data, this application is subject to the NIH Policy
content.label: content

content.text: for Data Management and Sharing and requires submission of a Data Management and Sharing Plan. If the proposed research in the
content.label: content

content.text: application will generate large-scale genomic data, the Genomic Data Sharing Policy also applies and should be addressed in this Plan.
content.label: content

content.text: Refer to the detailed instructions in the application guide for developing this plan as well as to additional guidance on sharing.nih.gov.
content.label: content

content.text: The Plan is recommended not to exceed two pages. Text in italics should be deleted (but this has not been done in the sample below).
content.label: content

content.text: There is no “form page” for the Data Management and Sharing Plan. The DMS Plan may be provided in the format shown below.
content.label: content

subsections.title: A. Types and amount of scientific data expected to be generated in the project:

content.text: Summarize the types and estimated amount of scientific data expected to be generated in the project.
content.label: content

content.text: Demographic, clinical, and MRI, H fMRS and fMRI imaging data will be acquired from 110 affected youth and
content.label: content

content.text: 110 matched healthy controls (described in detail in sections C.3 and C.4 of this application). All data will be de-
content.label: content

content.text: identified prior to receipt by the repository, but the information needed to generate a global unique identifier for
content.label: content

content.text: the NIMH Data Archive (NDA) will be collected for each subject.
content.label: content

subsections.title: B. Scientific data that will be preserved and shared, and the rationale for doing so:

content.text: Describe which scientific data from the project will be preserved and shared and provide the rationale
content.label: content

content.text: for this decision.
content.label: content

content.text: Sufficient data from this project will be preserved to enable sharing via NDA data of sufficient quality to validate
content.label: content

content.text: and replicate research findings described in the Aims. NIMH requires data measured from human subjects to be
content.label: content

content.text: shared using the NDA.
content.label: content

subsections.title: C. Metadata, other relevant data, and associated documentation:

content.text: Briefly list the metadata, other relevant data, and any associated documentation (e.g., study protocols
content.label: content

content.text: and data collection instruments) that will be made accessible to facilitate interpretation of the scientific
content.label: content

content.text: data.
content.label: content

content.text: In addition to the subject level data described above, all H fMRS and fMRI task related paradigm designs and
content.label: content

content.text: experiment definitions will be deposited in the NDA.
content.label: content

sections.title: Element 2: Related Tools, Software and/or Code:

content.text: State whether specialized tools, software, and/or code are needed to access or manipulate shared
content.label: content

content.text: scientific data, and if so, provide the name(s) of the needed tool(s) and software and specify how they
content.label: content

content.text: can be accessed.
content.label: content

content.text: The clinical data will be analyzed with custom Python code written using the statsmodels, numpy, and pandas
content.label: content

content.text: packages, all of which are freely available. H fMRS spectra will be analyzed with LCModel 6.3 software using
content.label: content

content.text: LCMgui, which is freely available. fMRI images will be analyzed using the SPM8 toolbox for MATLAB. While
content.label: content

content.text: MATLAB is commercial software, most universities have site licenses available and the SPM8 toolbox is free. It is
content.label: content

content.text: also possible that the toolbox might run in Octave, an open-source alternative to MATLAB, but we have not tried
content.label: content

content.text: it. All code will be shared on our GitHub lab website. The code can be found by searching for “labname” on
content.label: content

content.text: GitHub. The main readme.md file for the project will also include instructions and parameter choices for the GUI-
content.label: content

content.text: based analyses.
content.label: content

content.text: State what common data standards will be applied to the scientific data and associated metadata to
content.label: content

content.text: enable interoperability of datasets and resources and provide the name(s) of the data standards that
content.label: content

content.text: will be applied and describe how these data standards will be applied to the scientific data generated by
content.label: content

content.text: the research proposed in this project. If applicable, indicate that no consensus standards exist.
content.label: content

content.text: Participant age, sex, ethnicity, height, weight, socioeconomic status, and other demographic data will be
content.label: content

content.text: collected using the following instruments as defined in NDA:
content.label: question

content.text: 1) Research Subject and Pedigree (ndar_subject01)
content.label: content

content.text: 2) Demographics Short Form (demsf01)
content.label: content

content.text: 3) Ethnic Group Questionnaire (ethgrp01)
content.label: content

content.text: 4) Height and Weight (height_weight01)
content.label: content

content.text: 5) Hollingshead Socioeconomic Rating Scale (ses01)
content.label: content

content.text: 6) Pubertal Development Scale (pds01)
content.label: content

content.text: 7) Edinburgh Handedness Inventory (edinburgh_hand01)
content.label: content

content.text: 8) WASI-2 (wasi201).
content.label: content

content.text: In compliance with NOT-MH-20-067, the following data will be collected to facilitate aggregation of this data set
content.label: content

content.text: with other data sets:
content.label: question

content.text: 1) DSM Crosscutting for Youth (dsm5crossch01)
content.label: content

content.text: 2) RCADS-25 (rcads2501)
content.label: content

content.text: The clinical assessments we plan to collect for this study include:
content.label: question

content.text: 1) Kiddie-SADS-Present and Lifetime Version (ksads_pl01)
content.label: content

content.text: 2) Children’s Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (cybocs01)
content.label: content

content.text: 3) Schedule for Obsessive-Compulsive and Other Behavioral Syndromes (Hanna. Schedule for Obsessive-
content.label: content

content.text: Compulsive and Other Behavioral Syndromes, Ann Arbor: University of Michigan, 2010, new data
content.label: content

content.text: dictionary will be defined in NDA)
content.label: content

content.text: 4) Dimensional Obsessive Compulsive Scale (docs01)
content.label: content

content.text: 5) Yale Global Tic Severity Scale (yale01)
content.label: content

content.text: 6) Child Behavior Checklist (cbcl01)
content.label: content

content.text: 7) Multidimensional Anxiety Scale for Child Parent and Self (masc_p01)
content.label: content

content.text: 8) Conners 3 (conners3_ps01)
content.label: content

content.text: 9) Adolescent Depression Rating Scale (doi:10.1186/1471-244X-7-2, new data dictionary will be defined in
content.label: content

content.text: NDA)
content.label: content

content.text: H fMRS and fMRI data will be shared with the Image (image03), Imaging Work Flow (iwf01), and Imaging
content.label: content

content.text: Collection (imagingcollection01) data dictionaries as defined in NDA.
content.label: content

sections.title: Element 4: Data Preservation, Access, and Associated Timelines

subsections.title: A. Repository where scientific data and metadata will be archived:

content.text: Provide the name of the repository(ies) where scientific data and metadata arising from the project will
content.label: content

content.text: be archived; see Selecting a Data Repository).
content.label: content

content.text: All data will be deposited to NDA starting 12 months after the award begins and will be deposited every six
content.label: content

content.text: months thereafter following the usual NDA data submission dates.
content.label: content

subsections.title: B. How scientific data will be findable and identifiable:

content.text: Describe how the scientific data will be findable and identifiable, i.e., via a persistent unique identifier or
content.label: content

content.text: other standard indexing tools.
content.label: content

content.text: Data will be findable for the research community through the NDA Collection that will be established when this
content.label: content

content.text: application is funded. For all publications, an NDA study will be created. Each of those studies is assigned a
content.label: content

content.text: digital object identifier (DOI). This data DOI will be referenced in the publication to allow the research community
content.label: content

content.text: easy access to the exact data used in the publication.
content.label: content

subsections.title: C. When and how long the scientific data will be made available:

content.text: Describe when the scientific data will be made available to other users (i.e., no later than time of an
content.label: content

content.text: associated publication or end of the performance period, whichever comes first) and for how long data
content.label: content

content.text: will be available.
content.label: content

content.text: The research community will have access to data when the award ends. As required by NDA, studies will also
content.label: content

content.text: be created that contain the data used for every publication. Those studies will be shared when the pre-print is
content.label: content

content.text: available. NDA studies have digital object identifiers (DOI) to aid in findability. We will include that DOI in
content.label: content

content.text: relevant publications. NDA will make decisions about how long to preserve the data, but that data archive has
content.label: content

content.text: not deleted any deposited data up to now.
content.label: content

sections.title: Element 5: Access, Distribution, or Reuse Considerations

subsections.title: A. Factors affecting subsequent access, distribution, or reuse of scientific data:

content.text: NIH expects that in drafting Plans, researchers maximize the appropriate sharing of scientific data.
content.label: content

content.text: Describe and justify any applicable factors or data use limitations affecting subsequent access,
content.label: content

content.text: distribution, or reuse of scientific data related to informed consent, privacy and confidentiality
content.label: content

content.text: protections, and any other considerations that may limit the extent of data sharing. See Frequently
content.label: content

content.text: Asked Questions for examples of justifiable reasons for limiting sharing of data.
content.label: content

content.text: All research participants will be consented for broad data sharing.
content.label: content

subsections.title: B. Whether access to scientific data will be controlled:

content.text: State whether access to the scientific data will be controlled (i.e., made available by a data repository
content.label: content

content.text: only after approval).
content.label: content

content.text: To request access of the data, researchers will use the standard processes at NDA, and the NDA Data Access
content.label: content

content.text: Committee will decide which requests to grant. The standard NDA data access process allows access for one
content.label: content

content.text: year and is renewable.
content.label: content

subsections.title: C. Protections for privacy, rights, and confidentiality of human research participants:

content.text: If generating scientific data derived from humans, describe how the privacy, rights, and confidentiality of
content.label: content

content.text: human research participants will be protected (e.g., through de-identification, Certificates of
content.label: content

content.text: Confidentiality, and other protective measures).
content.label: content

content.text: The NDA GUID tool allows researchers to aggregate data from the same research participant without different
content.label: content

content.text: laboratories having to share personally identifiable information about that research participant. The NDA data
content.label: content

content.text: dictionaries do not permit personally identifiable information to be shared. NDA maintains a Certificate of
content.label: content

content.text: Confidentiality.
content.label: content

sections.title: Element 6: Oversight of Data Management and Sharing:

content.text: Describe how compliance with this Plan will be monitored and managed, frequency of oversight, and by
content.label: content

content.text: whom at your institution (e.g., titles, roles).
content.label: content

content.text: The Office of Sponsored Programs at University X that will be administering this award has created a data
content.label: content

content.text: management and sharing plan compliance system as part of their process for submitting the annual NIH progress
content.label: content

content.text: report. That Office is collecting information related to the number of research participants that are deposited
content.label: content

content.text: each reporting year. The Office of Sponsored Programs will also look for the NDA data DOIs from NDA Studies
content.label: content

content.text: and will include that information in the annual progress report.
content.label: content

sections.title: Validation Schedule (this section is required by NIMH)

content.text: If funded, within 6 months of the Notice of Award date we will submit a Data Submission Agreement signed by
content.label: content

content.text: the principal investigators and an institutional business official, as well as define and complete the Data Expected
content.label: content

content.text: section of this project. Uploads of all initial demographic, clinical, and raw structural MRI,
content.label: content

content.text: H fMRS and fMRI
content.label: content

content.text: research data will be completed using the second submission cycle deadline following the Notice of Award date.
content.label: content

content.text: Subsequent data uploads will be harmonized, validated, and submitted biannually on the standard January 15th
content.label: content

content.text: th
content.label: content

content.text: and July 15 submission deadlines.
content.label: content

content.text: We also plan to use the NDA validation tool as a quality control measure in the laboratory. The data manager in
content.label: content

content.text: charge of submitting data to NDA will help researchers in the group validate their data once every month.
